findings.claim: When rendering a page raises, PageImages.image() leaves the Page (and any Pixmap) alive in the traceback frame. They are freed when the caller's except block ends, after the lock was released, so their MuPDF finalizers run without PYMUPDF_LOCK.
findings.impact: A page that fails to render while an extraction or page OCR is running on another thread can make MuPDF run on two threads at once. pdf.py:60-62 says the other conversion can then fail over or return wrong text. This only happens on a render failure, which is rare.
findings.evidence: file_question.py:1045-1057: the `del pixmap, page` added in r7 runs only on the success path. If `page.get_pixmap(...)` or `pixmap.tobytes(...)` raises, the exception leaves `with self._locked()` (the lock is released at 1083) while `page` is still a local of the frame the traceback references. rag.py `_serve_page_request` handles it in `except Exception as exc: unavailable(page, type(exc).__name__)`; the frame, and with it `page`, is freed when `exc` is unbound at the end of that block, outside the lock. test_a_page_that_fails_to_render_takes_no_number_and_the_others_close_up exercises this path (get_pixmap raises RuntimeError) but never checks the lock.
findings.repro: not_reproduced. A mutation view: removing the r7 `del pixmap, page` line also survives every test, because no test records whether the lock is held when a Page or Pixmap is deallocated.

bucket_proposal.reason: I8 requires every PyMuPDF call made to render page images to run under PYMUPDF_LOCK. r6 accepted the finalizer drops of Page/Pixmap/Document as such calls (CR-1), and this failure path still drops them unlocked.

findings.proposed_fix: Wrap the body in try/finally inside the locked block (`page = pixmap = None` up front, `finally: del pixmap, page`) so both are dropped under the lock on every path.

findings.claim: _close_locked's `del document` does not drop the last reference to the Document. In the acquired branch, close()'s own local `document` keeps it alive until close() returns, after the lock was released. In the thread branch, Thread._args keeps it alive until run() finishes, also after the release. The Document's deallocation therefore always runs outside the lock, despite the docstring 'then drop it'.
findings.impact: After document.close() this is probably harmless, if a closed Document's dealloc no longer calls MuPDF. Still, the code and its comment claim a property ('dropped under the lock') that does not hold, and a later change could rely on it.
findings.evidence: file_question.py:1005-1013 (`document.close(); del document` deletes only the parameter binding); 1060-1067 (the caller's local `document` stays bound across `_close_locked(document, acquired=True)`); 1070-1072 (`threading.Thread(target=_close_locked, args=(document,))`, and CPython's Thread.run deletes `_target`/`_args` in its own finally, after the target returns). The hygiene test checks only that `Document.close` ran with the lock held, not the deallocation.

bucket_proposal.reason: No invariant breaks as long as close() releases MuPDF state; this is a fix whose stated mechanism does not do what it says.

findings.proposed_fix: Delete the ineffective `del document` and the 'then drop it' wording, or hand the only reference over (for example, pop it from a one-element list inside the locked block).

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: When a page request's lock budget has run out, its PDF is closed by a daemon thread that waits for PYMUPDF_LOCK with no time limit, keeping the file open until the extraction holding the lock finishes.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: Asking about PDF pages during a long extraction leaves one waiting thread and one open file per such request until the extraction ends; the user sees nothing.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: A section title cut to 60 characters after whitespace collapse may end in a space, which gives the contents line a double space before ' — '.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: An EPUB title whose 60th character is a space adds one stray space to a prompt line; it is invisible to the user.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: A title that is only markers or whitespace becomes None, and its contents line is written without a title, like a section with no stored title.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: Needs a stored title made only of bracketed numbers; the model sees no title for that section.

regression_risks: The new daemon close thread adds a lock waiter at question time. A thread that never gets the lock, for example one stuck behind a hung extraction, keeps its PDF open for the life of the process.

Tests now depend on the lock being a non-reentrant threading.Lock (the hygiene test acquires it on the main thread and expects close() to fail to take it); a switch to RLock would silently change both the test and close().

trajectory: There is one fix round since r6 (dd75388 moves the submodule to the fix commit; 99881c9 records r6). It adds the helper _contents_title, which reuses the existing marker removal; that adds no new state. It adds one branch to PageImages.close(): the early `return` that left the document to the collector becomes a deferred close on a daemon thread, which waits for the lock with no limit. It also adds the shared helper _close_locked. The record holds no earlier fix round, so no round repeats a branch an earlier one added. The close-path fix, however, has the same shape as the defect it fixes: it covers one exit (the success path and the timed-out close) and leaves a sibling exit (the render-failure traceback, CR7-1). The design is being patched path by path rather than by one structure that always drops MuPDF objects under the lock. Nothing was removed apart from the early return.
